turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response:
Hey, yeah, thanks for fitting me in. I'm, uh... I guess I'm here because things have just really been coming to a head lately. I just feel like I’m always running hot, you know? Like I’ve got this engine inside me and I literally cannot shut the motor off. 

And you’d think, right, being a firefighter—I’m 37, I’ve been doing this since I got my associate's degree, so I've been around the block—you’d think having a lot of energy would be a good thing in my line of work. And when the bells go off, sure, it’s great. But there’s actually a lot of downtime at the station, and lately, this whole... inability to just stop and take a breath has been getting me in real trouble at the firehouse. 

The captain actually pulled me aside recently because I'm just constantly going, and it's driving everyone crazy. The guys will be trying to rest or watch TV or eat a meal between calls, and I'm just pacing the bays, or I'm taking apart the chainsaws to clean them for the third time this week, or I'm sitting at the table bouncing my leg so hard the coffee spills. I just can't power down. It's exhausting for the rest of the crew, and honestly, it's exhausting for me, but if I try to just force myself to sit in the recliner like a normal person, it's like my skin starts buzzing and I physically have to get up and find something to do. So, yeah, I'm here because this internal motor just won't quit, and I need to figure out how to hit the brakes before it costs me my career.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes sitting at the table and bouncing his leg so hard that coffee spills.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states that when he tries to force himself to sit in a recliner, he physically has to get up.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient reports pacing the bays and feeling like his skin is buzzing, indicating severe restlessness.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient explicitly states he feels like he has an engine inside him, cannot shut the motor off, and is constantly going.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have this same kind of restlessness and difficulty sitting still back when you were a kid in school?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, man, yeah. If you ask my mom... well, she actually brought this up recently when I was venting to her about the captain getting on my case. She was like, 'You know you've been doing this since you were seven years old, right?' And it's true. Back in grade school, I was exactly the same way. I mean, it was a total nightmare for my teachers. 

My mom always says I was literally always out of my seat. Like, I couldn't just sit at the desk like the other kids. I'd be up sharpening my pencil, or walking over to the trash can, or I'd just be standing up at my desk while I was writing because sitting in that hard plastic chair felt like absolute torture. And the blurting things out—I just couldn't hold it in. The teacher would ask a question, and before she even finished her sentence, I'm just shouting the answer across the room. I wasn't trying to be a bad kid or disrespectful, the thought was just there in my head and it physically had to come out right that second. 

And the homework... God, the homework. It wasn't that I couldn't do it. My mom always reminds me, she says, 'You were so bright, you were smart enough to do all the work easily,' and I *did* do it half the time! But then I'd just lose it. It would completely vanish into this black hole at the bottom of my backpack, or I'd leave it on the kitchen counter, or drop it on the bus. So I'd constantly be getting these notes sent home in my folder. My mom dreaded checking my backpack at the end of the day because there was almost always a note from the teacher saying I wouldn't stay in my chair, or I interrupted the lesson again, or I didn't turn in the math worksheet that I had literally done the night before. It was just this endless cycle of notes sent home, even though everyone knew I was smart enough to get the material. 

So, yeah, this whole motor thing, the not being able to stop? It's definitely not new. It's just... I guess the stakes are a lot higher now, you know? Back then it was just a frustrated teacher and a note home, but now it's my actual livelihood and my crew.

symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient describes constantly losing their completed homework in their backpack, on the kitchen counter, or on the bus.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient notes that sitting still in a chair 'felt like absolute torture,' indicating intense internal restlessness.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient refers to their inability to sit still as 'this whole motor thing, the not being able to stop.'
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient admits to shouting out answers before the teacher had even finished asking the question.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient mentions receiving notes sent home from teachers because they 'interrupted the lesson again.'

Yeah, it's not just the physical motor running, if that's what you mean. It's... my brain just drops things constantly. I keep forgetting stuff that I honestly, genuinely mean to do. Like, okay, at the station we have all these mandatory training modules—OSHA updates, bloodborne pathogens, hazmat refreshers, that kind of thing. And they're not hard! But I will literally tell myself, 'I am going to sign off on this module right after morning check-offs,' and then I walk into the kitchen, someone asks me a question about the grocery fund, and the training module is just completely gone from my brain. Erased. The captain will have to track me down three days later, and I feel like an absolute idiot because I really did mean to do it. 

And it’s not just at work, it’s my personal life too. Calling people back? Forget about it. If I don't answer the phone when it rings, that person is probably never hearing from me again because the second the voicemail ends, the thought of returning the call just vanishes. And bills... man, I make decent money, I'm not broke, but I am constantly paying late fees. Just last month, I had the money sitting right there in my checking account, but I just completely forgot to actually log in and pay the electric bill until I got a final notice in the mail. It's just so frustrating because it's so avoidable, you know? 

But the worst part, the part that really makes me feel like I'm losing my edge, is the gear paperwork. We have to log our turnout gear inspections, right? It's a huge safety liability if we don't. I'll do the inspection, I'll have the actual paper in my hand, I'll set it on the bumper of the engine for one second to adjust my suspenders or tie my boot, and then I just walk away. Shift change rolls around, and the lieutenant is asking for my paperwork, and I have to go hunting for it in the bays. It's like I have a total sieve for a brain. People probably think I just don't care, or I'm being lazy, but I really do care, I just... I literally cannot hold onto a thought or a task long enough to finish it before it just slips away into the void.
